A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RISE-Judge research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and redrawn figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original RISE-Judge evaluations, training ablations, general-ability measurements and downstream policy-training experiments in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds PPE and AlpacaEval 2.0 evaluation results in Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: The data synthesis and filtering procedure, SFT warm-up, DPO enhancement and auxiliary NLL loss remain unchanged. Shortening repeated terminology and relocating the pipeline figure do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds PPE evaluation on MBPP, MATH and GPQA, plus AlpacaEval 2.0 evaluation. These extend the established judge and general-ability evaluation coverage; training datasets and all earlier benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged. The added benchmarks reuse existing comparators: CompassJudger-1-32B-Instruct, Self-taught-evaluator-llama3.1-70B and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct.

E3.justification: The added AlpacaEval 2.0 evaluation reports raw and length-controlled win rates and average response length. Existing training budgets, model configurations, decoding settings and evaluation procedures remain unchanged; detailed protocols for the new evaluations are not supplied.

E4.justification: The training-stage, data-volume, model-size and prompt-sensitivity ablations, along with the RewardBench case study, are retained. Appendix A.5 adds benchmark comparisons without introducing a separate ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new tables retain the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing results remain unchanged. New Table 4 reports PPE averages of 52.5 for RISE-Judge, 50.7 for CompassJudger and 44.6 for Self-taught-evaluator, although CompassJudger leads on GPQA. New Table 5 reports RISE versus Qwen raw win rates of 37.0 versus 30.0, length-controlled rates of 35.8 versus 37.4, and average lengths of 2058 versus 1808.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and definitions in Equations 1–4 are unchanged. No theorem, proof, formal assumption or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient two-stage training, RewardBench performance, general capabilities and downstream preference signals. The new benchmarks provide additional supporting evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 newly attributes longer responses to the CoT pattern learned during SFT and acknowledges a disadvantage under length control. Sections 4.2 and 4.5 add generalization interpretations, while Figure 3's caption newly emphasizes DPO's larger effect.

D1.justification: Training and sampling hyperparameters, model and dataset access links, prompt templates and training examples remain unchanged. The additional benchmark results introduce no substantive implementation or reproducibility details.

R1.justification: v2 adds Frick et al. (2024) for PPE and Dubois et al. (2024) for length-controlled AlpacaEval. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to earlier judge-training methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates affiliations and contact information, abbreviates repeated expansions of SFT, DPO, CoT and SOTA, and adds Appendix A.5 with short main-text references. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–5, redraws Figures 3–4 with revised colors, labels and axes, and relocates Figures 2 and 4. These are localized presentation changes; the redrawn ablation plots retain their numerical results.

improvement.justification: The new PPE and AlpacaEval comparisons modestly strengthen validation beyond v1's judging benchmark and expose a useful response-length tradeoff. The gain is limited by sparse evaluation details and overly broad superiority language: RISE trails CompassJudger on GPQA and Qwen on length-controlled win rate. The additional evidence improves the paper, but does not establish the uniform superiority suggested by the new discussion.
